items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And the next night I have a rhythm section. I have two — a great English jazz drummer, Steven Keogh, and Arnie Somogyi the bass player. And we’ll do some trio stuff.

ctx.x: Well I’m trying to bridge the gap between that era and the modern era, and how — I look at it from the utility of it. And I call it becoming a practical guitar player. But if you understand music and you understand all the parameters, the harmonic, the melodic, the contrapuntal, the tonal, the sonority of it, the ability of the guitar to integrate into an

ensemble, and the professional parameters of gigging, of making a living doing it — but also, when I refer to the real work starting — I mean Monday night next week I have a solo concert. And it’ll be a two hour concert. Whereas tomorrow night it’s 45 minutes and it’s like okay, the youth orchestra is on next. It’s stacked programming, like a festival. But when I have a solo concert — you know I’ve written 150 pieces for guitar. I’ve arranged probably that many again. You know I have to choose my repertoire based…
Well your career reminds me of Bucky Pizzarelli, who I’ve got to know fairly well. And what’s next, what’s tomorrow.
